<!-- BEAT 2 — Contesto: one neuron = one logistic -->

## *One neuron is one logistic — with $g$ free to be anything.*

![](../img/storyboard/sb-05_02.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

::: {.notes}
Callback strutturale esplicito a ch. 02 (la sigmoide come classificatore) ↔ il neurone artificiale. **Stessa macchina**: peso, somma pesata, attivazione. L'unica libertà nuova è la *forma* di $g$. Niente magia.
:::

## The artificial neuron

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

![](../img/neuron.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

Given inputs $a = (a_1, \ldots, a_n)$ and weights $w = (w_1, \ldots, w_n)$:

$$\text{out} = g\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_i \, w_i\right)$$

The chapter 2 logistic regression is the special case $g = \sigma$ (sigmoid). The artificial neuron *frees* $g$ — any **non-linear** and **differentiable** function will do.

:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Struttura *somma pesata + attivazione* = la logistica di ch. 02, ma $g$ libera (non solo $\sigma$).

- Vocabolario: *non-lineare* = forma di $g$ (non delle feature); *differenziabile* = serve al training (slide dopo).
:::

## Activation functions $g$ — common choices

The chapter requires $g$ to be **non-linear** *and* **differentiable**. Three canonical choices:

- **ReLU** (Rectified Linear Unit): $g(z) = \max(0, z)$ — the field's workhorse since the 2010s.
- **Sigmoid**: $g(z) = \sigma(z) = \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{-z}}$ — the same one from chapter 2 logistic regression.
- **Hyperbolic tangent**: $g(z) = \tanh(z) = \dfrac{e^z - e^{-z}}{e^z + e^{-z}}$.

All three satisfy the two requirements (ReLU is differentiable *almost* everywhere — the single point $z = 0$ is handled in practice with the sub-gradient $0$).

::: {.notes}
A voce (non sulla slide): ReLU = default hidden (cheap); sigmoid = output binario (prob.); tanh = sigmoid *centrato* in $[-1,+1]$.

- Anti-trabocchetto: ReLU non differenziabile in $z=0$, ma OK col sub-gradient $0$.
- ReLU è la canonical di item 02 e 03.
:::

<!-- BEAT 3 — Sfida / Dati: composition into layers -->

## *This is a deep network. Count them: twelve.*

![](../img/storyboard/sb-05_03.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

::: {.notes}
Il *gem*: rete $3 \to 2 \to 2 \to 1$ intera, si **contano** le connessioni una a una → **$12$**.

- Punto unico: "deep" = *stack*, non *magia*. Stesso ragionamento scala a $10^6$ pesi.
:::

## Composition — a fully-connected (MLP) network

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}

![](../img/mlp.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}

:::
::: {.column width="52%"}

Stack neurons into **layers**; feed the outputs of one layer as the inputs of the next:

$$a^{[l]} = g^{[l]}\!\left(W^{[l]} \, a^{[l-1]}\right)$$

where $W^{[l]}$ is the weight matrix of layer $l$.

A toy network $3 \to 2 \to 2 \to 1$ (no biases) has:

$$\underbrace{3 \cdot 2}_{\text{layer 1}} + \underbrace{2 \cdot 2}_{\text{layer 2}} + \underbrace{2 \cdot 1}_{\text{layer 3}} = \mathbf{12}\ \text{weights}.$$

**Twelve.** Drawable on a napkin.

:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Punto di svolta. Da landare: rete profonda = **composizione di oggetti familiari**, non nuovo oggetto matematico.

- $10^6$ pesi = stesso *ragionamento* con più righe, non *fenomeno* diverso.
- Il sommativo usa esattamente questa architettura $3 \to 2 \to 2 \to 1$.
:::

<!-- BEAT 4 — Nodo: loss landscape + gradient descent -->

## *Weights are coordinates. Loss is the height. Walk downhill.*

![](../img/storyboard/sb-05_04.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

::: {.notes}
Il *come impara*. Tripla metafora da insistere a voce: pesi = **coordinate**, errore = **altezza**, training = **camminare in discesa**.
:::

## Gradient descent — the training loop {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}

For a given training set, each combination of weights $W$ has a loss $L(W)$:

- $W$ = coordinates in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (where $d$ = number of weights).
- $L(W)$ = the *height* of the loss surface at $W$.

**Gradient descent**: walk downhill, one small step at a time:

$$W \leftarrow W - \eta \, \nabla_W L(W).$$

- $\nabla_W L(W)$ = direction of *steepest ascent*; we go *against* it.
- $\eta$ = **learning rate** = how big a step we take.

:::
::: {.column width="45%"}

![](../img/loss.png){fig-align="center" width="100%"}

![](../img/descent.gif){fig-align="center" width="100%"}

:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Sign ($-$) = scendi/sali; $\eta$ = lunghezza passo. Item 03 testa la coppia (distrattori sign × $\eta$).

- A voce: *backprop* = come si calcola $\nabla_W L$ (chain rule per strato), ma NON da derivare a mano in questo corso.
:::

## Why must $g$ be non-linear *and* differentiable?

Both requirements have **operational meaning** for the training procedure:

- **Non-linear** $g$ → the stack of layers is **more** than one big linear map. Otherwise $(g_1 \circ g_2 \circ g_3)(\cdots) = W x$ — one matrix multiplication, no matter how many layers. *No "deep".*
- **Differentiable** $g$ → the gradient $\nabla_W L(W)$ **exists** at every $W$. Otherwise: no direction to step in, and gradient descent has nothing to do. *No "learning".*

The two together: a *curved* loss landscape with a *slope at every point*. That's what makes descent possible.

::: {.notes}
Payoff Obj. 3: non-linearità → terreno *curvo*; differenziabilità → *pendenza ovunque*. Formulazione da portare fuori dall'aula.

- A voce (non sulla slide): perceptron anni '60 usava step di Heaviside → non differenziabile, training impossibile; servì il 1986 (Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams) con attivazioni *smooth*. È la lezione storica del DL.
:::

## *It's not magic — it's just bigger. But what about a chest X-ray?*

![](../img/storyboard/sb-05_06.png){fig-align="center" width="80%"}

::: {.notes}
Payoff: scatola *grande*, non *sigillata*. Atomi e meccanismo familiari.

- Gancio cap. 06: due dati clinici che NON sono vettori da $12$ — RX ($10^6$ pixel) ed ECG/pressione (sequenza variabile).
:::

## Pre-hook → chapter 6: unstructured data

Elena's stack of neurons can chew on any **vector** of inputs — age, BMI, a lab value — and learn from it.

But clinical data does **not** arrive as a tidy vector of length $12$:

- A chest X-ray is a **$1024 \times 1024$ image** — feed it raw to a fully-connected layer, and the first weight matrix alone holds over a million parameters *per neuron*.
- A blood-pressure trace is a **sequence**, varying in length — where do you even start?

The same logistic-stack-plus-descent machinery can survive the jump — but only with a clever rule about **which weights are shared**. That rule is the subject of chapter 6: **convolutional** networks for images, **recurrent** networks for sequences.

::: {.notes}
Pre-hook cap. 06. Salto qualitativo: i pesi non possono essere tutti diversi.

- Cliff-hanger lessicale: **convolutional / recurrent / weight sharing** (NON rivelare kernel/stride/time-step).
- A voce: il vincolo è forzato dal dato *clinico* (RX+ECG), non dalla matematica.
:::

<!-- Item 01 — MCQ — Neuron as generalised logistic -->

## Item 01 — Question {.smaller}

A clinical colleague tells you over coffee: *"an artificial neuron is just a fancy version of logistic regression."* Which one identifies the **single mathematical change** that turns a logistic regression into an artificial neuron?

- **A)** The sigmoid activation is replaced by **any non-linear, differentiable function** $g$ (ReLU, tanh, sigmoid as one special case). The weighted-sum structure $\sum_i a_i w_i$ is unchanged.
- **B)** The **input features** are squared ($a_i^2$ instead of $a_i$), so the neuron can model curved boundaries.
- **C)** The neuron carries **many weight vectors in parallel** instead of one, so it produces multiple outputs.
- **D)** The activation is **removed entirely**, so the neuron computes the bare $\sum_i a_i w_i$ — a *purely linear* version of logistic regression.

::: {.notes}
Item 01 — Comprehension / MCQ / low-medium · Obj. 1. File: `course/05-deep-learning/items/item_01_neuron-as-generalised-logistic_mcq.md`.

- Distrattori: B = kernel trick ch. 03 ("non-linearità nelle feature"); C = layer vs neurone; D = linearità collassante (peggiore).
:::

## Item 01 — Solution (write yours)

::: {.notes}
Lascia 30-45s. Misconception frequente: confondere C con A (layer vs singolo neurone — il neurone ha *un* vettore di pesi).
:::

## Item 01 — Solution

**Correct: A.** An artificial neuron is $\text{out} = g(\sum_i a_i w_i)$ where $g$ is non-linear and differentiable. The logistic regression of ch. 2 is the special case $g = \sigma$. The artificial neuron *frees* $g$ to any function satisfying the two requirements.

Why the distractors are wrong:

- **B** = **kernel trick of ch. 3** (non-linearity in the *features*, not the *activation*). Different mechanism.
- **C** = a **layer** of neurons, not a single neuron. The student has confused the atom with the molecule.
- **D** removes $g$ entirely → purely linear → stack collapses to one linear map. The *worst* answer: it is exactly what the chapter's requirement on $g$ forbids.

::: {.notes}
Discriminante = *swap dell'attivazione*, nient'altro. Riprendi la slide del neurone.

- Usa D come ponte a Obj. 3: la non-linearità rende lo stack ≠ mappa lineare.
:::

<!-- Item 02 — Applicativa — Forward pass + weight count -->

## Item 02 — Question {.smaller}

Network $3 \to 4 \to 2 \to 1$ (no biases): $3$ inputs · hidden 1 of $4$ neurons (ReLU) · hidden 2 of $2$ neurons (ReLU) · $1$ sigmoid output.

1. **Write the forward pass** in matrix form, $a^{[l]} = g^{[l]}(W^{[l]} a^{[l-1]})$, with explicit dimensions of each $W^{[l]}$.
2. **Count the total weights**, decomposed by layer.
3. Given $a^{[0]} = (1,\ 2,\ 0)$ and
$$W^{[1]} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2 & 0 \end{pmatrix},$$
compute $a^{[1]} = \text{ReLU}(W^{[1]} a^{[0]})$, **showing $z^{[1]} = W^{[1]} a^{[0]}$ first**.

::: {.notes}
Item 02 — Application / medium · Obj. 2 (forward pass + conta pesi + calcolo). Rubrica: `course/05-deep-learning/rubriche/rubrica_02_forward-pass-and-weight-count.md`.

- Architettura ≠ sommativo apposta ($3\to4\to2\to1$, $22$ pesi vs $3\to2\to2\to1$, $12$): misura il *processo*, non la memoria.
:::

## Item 02 — Solution (write yours)

::: {.notes}
Slide bianca, calcolo in 3 parti, ~5′.

- Teachable beat = sub-q 3: $z^{[1]}_4 = -2$ azzerato da ReLU. Chi scrive $a^{[1]}_4 = -2$ ha applicato una lineare, non ReLU.
:::

## Item 02 — Solution {.smaller}

**1.** Forward pass:

- $a^{[1]} = \text{ReLU}(W^{[1]} a^{[0]})$, $W^{[1]} \in \mathbb{R}^{4 \times 3}$, $a^{[1]} \in \mathbb{R}^4$.
- $a^{[2]} = \text{ReLU}(W^{[2]} a^{[1]})$, $W^{[2]} \in \mathbb{R}^{2 \times 4}$, $a^{[2]} \in \mathbb{R}^2$.
- $a^{[3]} = \sigma(W^{[3]} a^{[2]})$, $W^{[3]} \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times 2}$, $a^{[3]} \in \mathbb{R}$ — scalar output $\hat{y}$.

**2.** Weight count: $3 \cdot 4 + 4 \cdot 2 + 2 \cdot 1 = 12 + 8 + 2 = \mathbf{22}$.

**3.** Pre-activation $z^{[1]} = W^{[1]} a^{[0]} = (1,\ 2,\ 1,\ -2)$.
Apply ReLU element-wise: $a^{[1]} = (1,\ 2,\ 1,\ \mathbf{0})$ ← the **$-2$** is killed by the non-linearity.

::: {.notes}
Reveal: la **quarta componente** è il punto. $10^6$ pesi non cambiano il *processo*. La non-linearità fa lavoro visibile: un peso negativo = decisione "non attivare" che la rete impara.
:::

<!-- Item 03 — MCQ — One step of gradient descent -->

## Item 03 — Question {.smaller}

A toy neural network has **2 weights**, $w_1, w_2$. At the current weights
$$W_{\text{now}} = (3,\ 1)$$
the gradient is
$$\nabla_W L(W_{\text{now}}) = (2,\ -4).$$
Training uses **gradient descent with learning rate** $\eta = 0.5$.

After **one** update step, the new weight vector $W_{\text{next}}$ is:

- **A)** $(2,\ 3)$ &nbsp;·&nbsp; **B)** $(4,\ -1)$ &nbsp;·&nbsp; **C)** $(1,\ 5)$ &nbsp;·&nbsp; **D)** $(5,\ -3)$

::: {.notes}
Item 03 — Application / MCQ / medium · Obj. 3 (applica la formula). File: `course/05-deep-learning/items/item_03_gradient-descent-step_mcq.md`.

- Distrattori 2×2 (sign × $\eta$): A = giusto; B = sign-flip (ascent); C = $\eta$ scordato (step troppo grande); D = entrambi sbagliati.
:::

## Item 03 — Solution (write yours)

::: {.notes}
Lascia 30-45s. Discriminante = formula $W \leftarrow W - \eta \nabla L$.

- Se esitano tra A e C, richiama la slide di gradient descent ($\eta$ = step size).
:::

## Item 03 — Solution

**Correct: A.**
$$\begin{aligned}
W_{\text{next}} &= W_{\text{now}} - \eta \, \nabla_W L \\
&= (3,\ 1) - 0.5 \cdot (2,\ -4) \\
&= (3,\ 1) - (1,\ -2) \;=\; (2,\ 3).
\end{aligned}$$

Why the distractors are wrong:

- **B** = sign-flip → **gradient ascent**, walks *uphill* (increases the loss).
- **C** = forgot $\eta$ → *direction* is right (downhill), but the *step size* is wrong. A step too big can overshoot the minimum, oscillate, or diverge. **$\eta$ controls how far you move.**
- **D** = both errors at once. Sign wrong + step too big.

::: {.notes}
Take-away: sign = downhill/uphill; $\eta$ = step size. Distractor C è il più ricco: apre "cosa è $\eta$?" (overshoot, oscillation).

- A voce: "$\eta$ piccolo → lento ma stabile; grande → veloce ma rischioso" = prima intuizione hyperparameter del DL.
:::

## Summative — *Open the box: $3 \to 2 \to 2 \to 1$* {.inverse .smaller background-color="#1F4257"}

Network: **$3 \to 2 \to 2 \to 1$** (no biases), hidden = ReLU, output = sigmoid. *The diagram you'll work on:*

![](../img/storyboard/sb-05_05_labeled.png){fig-align="center" width="58%"}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

**On the network (top half of the board):**

(i) Write the **forward pass** equations layer by layer, $a^{[l]} = g^{[l]}(W^{[l]} a^{[l-1]})$.

(ii) **Count the total weights** — show $\square + \square + \square = ?$.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

**On the loss-landscape contour map (bottom half):**

(iii) Circle the arrow $A / B / C / D$ in the **steepest-descent** direction; justify in one sentence (what makes it the right one — and what's wrong with each of the other three).

(iv) One sentence on $g$: the **two properties** it must have, and *why each matters* for (iii).

:::
:::

**Two live polls:** *"Total weights?"* ($8 / 12 / 17 / 24$) · *"Steepest descent step?"* ($A / B / C / D$).

::: {.notes}
Sommativo, ultimi ~9′ (min 16-25). Timing: ~1′ leggi+apri poll · ~3′ forward pass+conta pesi (poll 1 $\ge 80\%$) · ~2′ freccia+1-sentence (poll 2 $\ge 80\%$) · ~1′ 1-sentence su $g$ · ~2′ reveal. Banco unico condiviso.

- Reveal: "$12$ pesi che camminano in discesa — Elena guarda dentro la scatola".
- Teachable bias Poll 1: il badge "$17$" di `sb-05_03.png` NON è sbagliato — *pesi* (archi) $=12$, *parametri* (+5 bias) $=17$. Ponte a ch. 06 (weight sharing).
- 4 arrows Poll 2: corretta = perpendicolare al contour verso il minimo; le altre = sign-flip uphill, tangente al contour, obliqua a $\sim 45°$.
- Reveal completo: `course/05-deep-learning/objectives.md`.
:::

## Summative — Solution (write yours)

::: {.notes}
Slide bianca, 4 sub-task; riempio la shared board mano a mano.

- Distrattori Poll 1 (spiegare, non penalizzare): $8$ = scordato $2\to2$; $17$ = +5 bias; $24$ = doppio conteggio (in+out).
:::

## Summative — Solution {.smaller}

**(i)** Forward pass:
$$a^{[1]} = \text{ReLU}(W^{[1]} a^{[0]}),\quad a^{[2]} = \text{ReLU}(W^{[2]} a^{[1]}),\quad a^{[3]} = \sigma(W^{[3]} a^{[2]}).$$

**(ii)** Weight count: $3 \cdot 2 + 2 \cdot 2 + 2 \cdot 1 = 6 + 4 + 2 = \mathbf{12}$.

**(iii)** **Anti-gradient direction** — perpendicular to the local loss contour **and** pointing toward the minimum. The loss decreases *fastest* along $-\nabla_W L$. Why the other three arrows fail: *perpendicular-uphill* = the gradient itself (sign-flip, ascent); *tangent to the contour* = moves along the same loss level (perpendicular $\ne$ descent); *oblique at $\sim 45°$* = does decrease the loss, but **not at the maximum rate** — gradient descent specifically asks for the *steepest* one.

**(iv)** $g$ must be **non-linear** (so the stack does not collapse to one linear map) **and** **differentiable** (so $\nabla_W L$ exists at every $W$ and descent has a direction to take).

*Take-home:* a deep network is a **composition** of generalised logistic units, trained by **gradient descent** on a loss landscape. The black box is *big*, not *sealed* — Elena can read its parts.

::: {.notes}
Reveal: chiude il cliff-hanger di ch. 04 — il *come* = composizione + discesa, niente magia.

- Pre-hook ch. 06: RX ed ECG non sono vettori da $12$ → serve weight sharing.
- Chiudi con: *"It's not magic — it's just bigger. But what about a chest X-ray?"*
:::
